newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Przymierze cleared to launch two more funds.
newsitem.headline: Polish Przymierze cleared to launch two more funds.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) has cleared mutual fund company Przymierze Towarzystwo Funduszy Powierniczych SA to launch two more funds, the KPW said in a statement on Thursday.
Przymierze president Tomasz Bankowski said that one of the funds, Fundusz Powierniczy Ochrony Kapitalu Eurofundusz 3, would be characterised by its low commissions.
He said the second, Akcyjny Indeksowy Fundusz Powierniczy Eurofundusz 4, would reflect the growth of the Warsaw bourse's main WIG index.
Bankowski said the funds would start selling units in September and would be geared toward institutional investors.

Przymierze, 51-percent owned by Polish state-owned Bank Pekao SA and 49-percent owned by the U.S.'s Alliance Capital Management LP, already runs a balanced fund and an aggressive stock-based fund in Poland.
